label: <DEL> step of long sequences that start with j (about to output j)
explanation: Fires almost only on the delimiter step (98% of activation mass), when the first original token, which is output at <DEL>, is j (87% of mass, 45x lift). Rate goes up with sequence length: almost nothing for L<=5, rare at L=6, highest at L=8-9. Weaker firing at <DEL> when the first token is p or u (about 3% of mass each). There are tiny activations on the last one or two original tokens of long j-initial sequences. It never fires during the copy phase. Precision is limited: many long j-initial sequences do not activate it, and no simple content condition I tested (m present, early digits) separated them. The top examples often have m or a digit at positions 1-3, but that did not hold up as a predictor.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=j (+5.99), orig0=p (+2.92), orig2=m (+2.89), phase=1 & out_tok=j (+2.89), orig3=m (+2.88), orig1=p (+2.87). Lower it: phase=2 (-6.32), orig6=- (-3.79), orig5=- (-3.58), orig1=l (-2.78).
